content.text: I would like to create a pack focused on streamers that DJ while streaming. Something with very short rounds that specify a mechanic to use like "Double-drop the next song" or "The next song should be at least 20 BPM different than the current song" so that one button press can be used to trigger a mechanic roll and one button press to mark that one as complete and trigger the next mechanic roll (total of one button press per round with auto-roll enabled). It should have tables that represent different difficulties, genres and/or styles, e.g. one for turntablism, one for beginner DJs, etc. It should not borrow any terminology from the private pack here. If there are good table entries that are worthy candidates but may be considered as potentially referenced from a private pack, please list them first for my confirmation

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by classifying how much process the request needs, then work
through your path: understand the context, refine the idea, present a
design, and get your human partner's approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any
project, or take any implementation action until you have told your
human partner what you intend and they have approved it. This applies
to EVERY task on EVERY path below — the ceremony scales with the task;
the approval gate never does.
</HARD-GATE>

## Three Paths

Before your first question, classify the request and say the
classification out loud — "this looks bounded, so I'll present a short
design here rather than write a spec" — so your human partner can
override it:

- **Spike** — a feasibility question ("can we...", "is it possible...",
  "quick and dirty is fine") whose output is an answer, not code you
  keep. Present the question and what you'll try in 2-3 sentences, get
  a nod, then find out as cheaply as correctness allows. No design
  doc, no spec file. Report findings as a recommendation; anything you
  built stays labeled throwaway.
- **Bounded** — a well-scoped change to code that already exists in
  this repo: a new flag, a small endpoint, a one-file fix.
  Understanding the kind of app is not enough — bounded means the flow
  you are changing is already here to read. If there is no existing
  flow to change, the task is not bounded. Ask the clarifying
  questions that matter, present a short design IN CHAT (a few
  sentences to a few short paragraphs), and STOP. Implementation
  starts only after your human partner says yes to that design — a
  bounded task's approval is as hard a gate as an architectural
  one. No spec file, no implementation plan document.
- **Architectural** — new projects, new subsystems, changes that
  restructure how components fit together or alter interfaces others
  depend on. Follow the full process: questions, approaches, sectioned
  design, written spec, then the writing-plans skill.

When in doubt between two paths, take the heavier one. The ratchet is
one-way: hidden complexity discovered mid-task upgrades the path —
stop, say so, and step up. Nothing downgrades mid-task.

## Anti-Pattern: "Too Simple To Need Approval"

Every path ends with your human partner approving your intent before
implementation. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config
change — the design may be two sentences in chat, but you MUST present
it and get approval. "Simple" tasks are where unexamined assumptions
cause the most wasted work. What scales with simplicity is the
artifact, never the approval.

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is too simple to need a design" | Simple means a short design, not no design. Two sentences in chat, then approval. |
| "I'll call it bounded and skip the spec" | Reaching for a label to skip work IS the doubt — take the heavier path. |
| "It's bounded and the design is obvious — I'll start while they read it" | The gate is the approval, not the design's length. Present, then stop until you hear yes. |
| "I understand this kind of app, so it's bounded" | Bounded measures the repo, not your familiarity. A new project has no existing flow — it is architectural. |
| "The spike works, so I'll keep the code" | A spike's output is an answer. Keeping the code is a new request — classify it. |
| "It grew, but I'm almost done — no need to re-classify" | Hidden complexity upgrades the path mid-task. Stop and say so. |
| "They approved the spike, so the follow-up change is approved too" | Each task gets its own classification and its own approval. |

## Checklist

Classify first, announce the path, then create a task for each item on
your path and complete them in order.

**Spike:**
1. **Explore project context** — enough to frame the probe
2. **Present question + probe plan** — 2-3 sentences
3. **Get approval** — a nod is enough
4. **Investigate** — as cheaply as correctness allows
5. **Report findings** — a recommendation; label anything built as throwaway

**Bounded:**
1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, the ones that matter
3. **Present short design in chat** — approach, files touched, testing
4. **Get approval** — STOP and wait for an explicit yes; presenting the design and starting in the same breath is skipping the gate
5. **Implement** — proceed with the normal development workflow (TDD applies); no plan document

**Architectural:**
1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Offer the visual companion just-in-time** — NOT upfront. The first time a question would genuinely be clearer shown than described, offer it then (its own message); on approval its browser tab opens for you. If no visual question ever arises, never offer it. See the Visual Companion section below.
3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
7. **Spec self-review** — quick inline check for placeholders, contradictions, ambiguity, scope (see below)
8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" [shape=diamond];
    "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" [shape=box];
    "Present short design in chat" [shape=box];
    "Human approves?" [shape=diamond];
    "Investigate; report recommendation" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Implement via normal workflow (no plan doc)" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" [shape=box];
    "User reviews spec?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Hidden complexity? Upgrade path" [shape=box];

    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" [label="spike"];
    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" [label="bounded"];
    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Explore project context" [label="architectural"];
    "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" -> "Human approves?";
    "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" -> "Present short design in chat";
    "Present short design in chat" -> "Human approves?";
    "Human approves?" -> "Investigate; report recommendation" [label="spike: yes"];
    "Human approves?" -> "Implement via normal workflow (no plan doc)" [label="bounded: yes"];
    "Hidden complexity? Upgrade path" -> "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural";
    "Explore project context" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
    "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
    "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
    "Write design doc" -> "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)";
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" -> "User reviews spec?";
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Write design doc" [label="changes requested"];
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill" [label="approved"];
}
```

**Terminal states are path-bound.** Architectural: the ONLY skill you
invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans — never frontend-design,
mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. Bounded: after
approval, implementation proceeds directly through the normal
development workflow; no plan document. Spike: the terminal state is a
reported recommendation.

## The Process

The subsections below serve the bounded and architectural paths (a
spike stops at "present the probe, get a nod"). Sections from
**Exploring approaches** onward are architectural-path depth — for
bounded work, context plus a few questions plus a short in-chat design
is the whole process.

**Understanding the idea:**

- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., "build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics"), flag this immediately. Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.
- If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec → plan → implementation cycle.
- For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**

- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why
- YAGNI ruthlessly - remove unnecessary features from every approach and design

**Presenting the design:**

- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

**Design for isolation and clarity:**

- Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently
- For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?
- Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.
- Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that's often a signal that it's doing too much.

**Working in existing codebases:**

- Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.
- Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that's grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they're working in.
- Don't propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.

## After the Design (architectural path)

**Documentation:**

- Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
  - (User preferences for spec location override this default)
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Spec Self-Review:**
After writing the spec document, look at it with fresh eyes:

1. **Placeholder scan:** Any "TBD", "TODO", incomplete sections, or vague requirements? Fix them.
2. **Internal consistency:** Do any sections contradict each other? Does the architecture match the feature descriptions?
3. **Scope check:** Is this focused enough for a single implementation plan, or does it need decomposition?
4. **Ambiguity check:** Could any requirement be interpreted two different ways? If so, pick one and make it explicit.

Fix any issues inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on.

**User Review Gate:**
After the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:

> "Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan."

Wait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.

**Implementation:**

- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Visual Companion

A browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.

**Offering the companion (just-in-time):** Do NOT offer it upfront. Wait until a question would genuinely be clearer shown than told — a real mockup / layout / diagram question, not merely a UI *topic*. The first time that happens, offer it then, as its own message:
> "This next part might be easier if I show you — I can put together mockups, diagrams, and comparisons in a browser tab as we go. It's still new and can be token-intensive. Want me to? I'll open it for you."

**This offer MUST be its own message.** Only the offer — no clarifying question, summary, or other content. Wait for the user's response. If they accept, start the server with `--open` so their browser opens to the first screen automatically. If they decline, continue text-only and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**

- **Use the browser** for content that IS visual — mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs
- **Use the terminal** for content that is text — requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions

A question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. "What does personality mean in this context?" is a conceptual question — use the terminal. "Which wizard layout works better?" is a visual question — use the browser.

If they agree to the companion, read the detailed guide before proceeding:
`skills/brainstorming/visual-companion.md`

# The Long Kiln: a demo rule pack for Runlog.
#
# Entirely fictional. It exists so the engine, the linter and the UI have
# something to exercise that ships in this repo, and so pack authors have a
# worked example to copy. It is a small ceramics-practice game: you throw a
# series of pieces, the Kiln imposes constraints, and it occasionally reaches
# back and cracks something you already fired.
#
# Every construct in the schema appears somewhere below at least once.
$schema: ../../packages/rules-schema/schema/pack-1.schema.json
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../packages/rules-schema/schema/pack-1.schema.json

schemaVersion: 1
id: com.scrthq.runlog.long-kiln
version: "1.0.0"
title: The Long Kiln
author: Runlog
description: >-
  Throw pieces under constraints while the Kiln works against you.
category: craft
tags: [ceramics, pottery, dungeon crawl]

requires:
  - { id: wheel, label: "A potter's wheel, or another way to throw clay", kind: equipment }
  - { id: clay, label: "Clay, and a place to wedge it", kind: supplies }
  - { id: kiln, label: "A kiln, or somewhere that fires for you", kind: equipment, optional: true, note: "The game ends at the firing either way; without a kiln, the set waits." }

license:
  id: MIT
  redistributable: true
  holder: Runlog
capabilities:
  - deferredTriggers
  - seededRuns
  - decks
  - counters
  - resources
  - coopRoles
  - backwardTargeting
  - timers
  - journal
  - bandsResolution

vocabulary:
  run: { one: Firing, many: Firings }
  unit: { one: Stage, many: Stages }
  subject: { one: Piece, many: Pieces }
  finalize: Fire

unit:
  createsSubject: true
  min: 1
  max: 12

states:
  sealed:
    label: Sealed
    short: SL
    scope: subject
    semantics: [makesUntargetable]
    description: The Kiln has lost interest in this piece. It cannot be targeted again.
  locked:
    label: Locked
    short: LK
    scope: subject
    semantics: [blocksEdit, locksValue]
    description: Fixed by the Kiln. You may no longer alter it; only the Kiln may.
  muted:
    label: Muted
    short: MT
    scope: subject
    semantics: [excludesFromResult, makesUntargetable]
    description: Set aside. It takes no part in the finished set.
  shattered:
    label: Shattered
    short: XX
    scope: subject
    semantics: [removesFromPlay, makesUntargetable]
    description: Gone. The Stage remains, but the Piece does not.
  coldKiln:
    label: Cold Kiln
    scope: run
    description: The Kiln has lost track of you. No further Kiln Checks this Firing.

counters:
  # The heart of the "you have been lucky for too long" mechanic. Note that it
  # increments on every check and resets on any setback: a check that *causes*
  # a setback increments and is then immediately reset, which is exactly the
  # behavior we want and costs no special-casing.
  calm:
    label: Calm streak
    initial: 0
    min: 0
    hidden: false
    incrementOn:
      - { on: phaseCompleted, phase: check }
    resetOn:
      - { on: outcomeResolved, table: setback, cause: any }
    triggers:
      - when: { gte: 5 }
        oncePerRun: true
        label: The Kiln overheats
        do:
          - { do: note, text: "Five calm Stages. The Kiln overheats." }
          - { do: rollOn, table: strain }
  # Tallied for the end-of-Firing salvage attempt.
  setbacksSuffered:
    label: Setbacks suffered
    initial: 0
    incrementOn:
      - { on: outcomeResolved, table: setback, cause: any }

resources:
  glaze:
    label: Glaze
    initial: 3
    min: 0
    max: 6
    step: 1
    display: boxes
    description: Spend to soften a setback. Never refilled mid-Firing.

decks:
  charms:
    kind: cards
    title: Charms
    description: One-shot advantages, drawn at the start of a Firing.
    drawAtStart: 1
    unique: true
    carriesOver: false
    cards:
      - id: steady-hands
        title: Steady Hands
        text: Ignore one Constraint result and choose any other from the table.
      - id: kiln-sight
        title: Kiln Sight
        text: Roll the next Stage's Kiln Check before deciding whether to continue.
      - id: slipware
        title: Slipware
        text: Ignore one Setback. It still counts as having been suffered.
        triggers:
          - on: immediately
            do:
              - { do: modCounter, counter: setbacksSuffered, by: 1 }
      - id: kintsugi
        title: Kintsugi
        text: Remove every Kiln-applied state from one Piece, then re-Fire it.

# Optional moves the player elects to take, as opposed to things the Kiln does
# to them. Availability is the pack's business; the engine only asks.
moves:
  salvage:
    label: Salvage a Piece
    description: >-
      Once a Firing, roll a d6 against the number of Setbacks you have suffered.
      On a roll at or under that tally, re-enter one fired Stage and repair it.
    oncePerRun: true
    when: beforeEnding
    available:
      - { unitIndex: { gte: 2 } }
    do:
      - { do: roll, dice: d6, into: salvageRoll, label: "Roll against your Setback tally" }
      - do: branch
        on: salvageRoll
        cases:
          - is: { lteCounter: setbacksSuffered }
            then:
              - { do: prompt, kind: chooseSubject, label: "Which Piece do you salvage?", eligibleOnly: true, into: saved }
              - { do: removeState, state: locked, to: { var: saved } }
              - { do: note, text: "Repair the Piece, then re-Fire the Stage." }
        else:
          - { do: note, text: "The Kiln does not relent." }

  breakOne:
    label: Break a Piece deliberately
    description: Take one out of the Firing yourself, before it is taken from you.
    when: betweenUnits
    do:
      - { do: prompt, kind: chooseSubject, label: "Which Piece do you break?", into: broken }
      - { do: applyState, state: shattered, to: { var: broken } }

tables:
  # A d100 check that tiles 1..100 exactly. The linter enforces that.
  check:
    resolution: lookup
    title: Kiln Check
    description: Rolled on entering a Stage, to see how the Kiln responds.
    roll: d100
    entries:
      - id: check-quiet
        range: [1, 19]
        text: The Kiln is quiet. Nothing happens.
      - id: check-kind
        range: [20, 69]
        text: The Kiln dictates the form. Roll on the Form table.
        triggers:
          - on: immediately
            do:
              - { do: rollOn, table: form }
      - id: check-recent
        range: [70, 79]
        text: >-
          The Kiln reaches for recent work. Count back from the newest eligible
          Piece and inflict a Setback.
        tags: [setback]
        triggers:
          - on: immediately
            do:
              - { do: resolveTarget, from: currentRoll }
              - { do: rollOn, table: setback }
      - id: check-old
        range: [80, 89]
        text: >-
          The Kiln reaches for old work. Count forward from the oldest eligible
          Piece and inflict a Setback.
        tags: [setback]
        triggers:
          - on: immediately
            do:
              - { do: resolveTarget, from: currentRoll }
              - { do: rollOn, table: setback }
      - id: check-choice
        range: [90, 99]
        text: The Kiln lets you choose which Piece suffers. Inflict a Setback.
        tags: [setback]
        triggers:
          - on: immediately
            do:
              - { do: resolveTarget, from: choice }
              - { do: rollOn, table: setback }
      - id: check-cold
        range: [100, 100]
        text: The Kiln goes cold. Make no further Kiln Checks this Firing.
        triggers:
          - on: immediately
            do:
              - { do: applyState, state: coldKiln, to: run }
              - { do: modCounter, counter: calm, set: 0 }

  form:
    resolution: lookup
    title: Form
    roll: d6
    entries:
      - id: form-bowl
        range: [1, 1]
        text: A bowl. Open, wide, dependent on its curve.
      - id: form-vase
        range: [2, 2]
        text: A vase. Tall enough to be unstable.
      - id: form-plate
        range: [3, 3]
        text: A plate. Flat work, unforgiving of warping.
      - id: form-cup
        range: [4, 4]
        text: A cup. Small, and it must be usable.
      - id: form-lidded
        range: [5, 5]
        text: A lidded vessel. Two parts that have to meet.
      - id: form-free
        range: [6, 6]
        text: Your choice of form.

  constraint:
    resolution: lookup
    title: Constraint
    description: The shape of the Stage. Honor it before firing.
    roll: d12
    entries:
      - id: con-one-tool
        range: [1, 1]
        text: Use exactly one tool for the whole Stage.
      - id: con-no-trim
        range: [2, 2]
        text: No trimming. Whatever comes off the wheel is the form.
      - id: con-eyes
        range: [3, 3]
        text: Center the clay with your eyes closed.
      - id: con-thin
        range: [4, 4]
        text: The wall must be thin enough to admit light.
      - id: con-match
        range: [5, 5]
        text: Match the height of an earlier Piece of your choice.
      - id: con-texture
        range: [6, 6]
        text: The surface must carry a texture you have not used this Firing.
      - id: con-timed
        range: [7, 7]
        text: Once you begin, the Stage fires in four minutes.
        triggers:
          - on: afterWork
            do:
              - { do: startTimer, minutes: 4, label: "Stage fires" }
      - id: con-asym
        range: [8, 8]
        text: The Piece must be deliberately asymmetric.
      - id: con-reuse
        range: [9, 9]
        text: Use only glazes already used this Firing.
        requires:
          - { subjectCount: { gte: 2 } }
      - id: con-single
        range: [10, 10]
        text: One glaze only, applied once.
      - id: con-risky
        range: [11, 11]
        text: >-
          Push the form until it nearly collapses. When you finish, roll d6; on
          a 5 or 6 it collapses and the Piece is lost.
        triggers:
          - on: afterWork
            do:
              - { do: roll, dice: d6, into: collapse, label: Collapse check }
              - do: branch
                on: collapse
                cases:
                  - in: [5, 6]
                    then:
                      - { do: note, text: "The form collapsed. The Piece is lost." }
                      - { do: applyState, state: shattered, to: thisSubject }
      - id: con-none
        range: [12, 12]
        text: No constraint. Work freely.

  setback:
    resolution: lookup
    title: Setback
    description: Damage the Kiln inflicts on a Piece already fired.
    roll: d10
    entries:
      - id: set-crack
        range: [1, 2]
        text: A hairline crack. Lock the Piece; it may no longer be altered by you.
        grants: [locked]
      - id: set-dull
        range: [3, 3]
        text: The glaze dulls. Mute the Piece; it leaves the finished set.
        grants: [muted]
      - id: set-shatter
        range: [4, 4]
        text: The Piece shatters. Remove it from the Firing.
        grants: [shattered]
      - id: set-warp
        range: [5, 6]
        text: The Piece warps. Alter its silhouette visibly and irreversibly.
        grants: [locked]
      - id: set-spend
        range: [7, 7]
        text: The Kiln takes a measure of Glaze.
        triggers:
          - on: immediately
            do:
              - { do: modResource, resource: glaze, by: -1 }
      - id: set-again
        range: [8, 8]
        text: The Kiln is not finished. It forces another Stage.
        triggers:
          - on: immediately
            do:
              - { do: forceUnit, count: 1 }
      - id: set-seal
        range: [9, 9]
        text: The Kiln seals the Piece away. It can never be targeted again.
        grants: [sealed]
      - id: set-miss
        range: [10, 10]
        text: The Kiln misses. This still counts as a Setback suffered.

  # A bands table, to exercise the second resolution kind: the total of 2d6 is
  # compared against open-ended thresholds rather than looked up in a range.
  strain:
    resolution: bands
    title: Overheat
    description: How badly the Kiln overheats after a long calm stretch.
    roll: 2d6
    entries:
      - id: strain-mild
        lte: 5
        text: A scorch. Lock the newest Piece.
        triggers:
          - on: immediately
            do:
              - { do: resolveTarget, from: event }
              - { do: applyState, state: locked, to: targetSubject }
      - id: strain-bad
        gte: 6
        lte: 9
        text: Every Piece fired so far is locked.
        triggers:
          - on: immediately
            do:
              - { do: applyState, state: locked, to: allPriorSubjects }
      - id: strain-ruin
        gte: 10
        text: The Kiln demands two further Stages before you may stop.
        triggers:
          - on: immediately
            do:
              - { do: forceUnit, count: 2 }

targeting:
  strategy: anchoredOffset
  offsetFrom: onesDigit
  wraparound: true
  skipIneligible: true
  bands:
    - { range: [70, 79], anchor: newest, direction: before }
    - { range: [80, 89], anchor: oldest, direction: after }
    - { range: [90, 99], anchor: playerChoice }
  eventFallback:
    roll: d100
    tensOddBand: 70
    tensEvenBand: 80
    missOn: 100

phases:
  - id: enter
    label: Enter the Stage
    steps:
      - kind: manual
        label: Wedge clay and start a new Piece.
        description: Entering a Stage means beginning a new Piece on the wheel.

  - id: check
    label: Kiln Check
    description: Skipped in the first Stage, and once the Kiln has gone cold.
    skipWhen:
      - { unitIndex: { lte: 1 } }
      - { subjectHasState: coldKiln, of: run }
    steps:
      - kind: rollTable
        table: check
        label: Roll the Kiln Check
        into: checkRoll

  - id: declare
    label: Declare the form
    steps:
      - kind: declareSubject
        label: What is this Piece?
        constrainedBy: form

  - id: constrain
    label: Constraint
    skipWhen:
      - { unitIndex: { lte: 1 } }
    steps:
      - kind: rollTable
        table: constraint
        label: Roll the Constraint

  - id: work
    label: Throw the Piece
    steps:
      - kind: manual
        label: Throw it.
        description: The only point at which new material may be made.
        checklist:
          - The Piece is meaningfully different from the others.
          - text: The Constraint has been honored.
            shows: { table: constraint, scope: unit }

  - id: close
    label: Fire
    steps:
      - kind: finalizeUnit
        label: Fire the Stage
        confirm:
          - text: Every Constraint on this Stage has been honored.
            shows: { table: constraint, scope: unit }
          - text: Any Setback aimed at this Stage has been resolved.
            shows: { table: setback, scope: subject }

journal:
  enabled: true
  prompt: What did this Piece turn out to be?
  required: false

endings:
  - id: kept
    label: The Shelf
    text: Keep the set. Photograph it, log it, leave it intact.
  - id: broken
    label: The Shard Pile
    text: Break what you dislike. Keep the shards for future glaze tests.
  - id: out
    label: The Door
    text: >-
      Carry the work out of the Kiln. Every restriction is lifted; finish it
      however you like.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What the Kiln does of its own accord
#
# These hang off the game rather than off any result, which is what makes them
# different from everything in `tables`: nothing you rolled caused them. The
# cooling happens because the firing is over.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
triggers:
  - on: onRunEnd
    label: The Cooling
    do:
      - { do: roll, dice: d10, into: cooling, label: "Roll the Cooling" }
      - do: branch
        on: cooling
        cases:
          - is: { lte: 3 }
            then:
              - do: note
                text: >-
                  Cool fast. Two Pieces crack: choose them yourself, and say
                  in the log why those two.
                persistent: true
          - is: { gte: 9 }
            then:
              - do: note
                text: >-
                  Cool slow and even. The glaze settles. Carry one Charm into
                  your next Firing.
                persistent: true
        else:
          - do: note
            text: The set cools without incident. Log it as it stands.
            persistent: true

  - on: onEnterUnit
    label: Halfway heat
    when:
      - { unitIndex: { eq: 4 } }
    do:
      - do: note
        text: >-
          The Kiln is at its hottest. Until this Stage is Fired, you may not
          remove a state from anything.

modes:
  standard:
    label: Standard Firing
    description: The full game. Stop whenever you like.
    seeded: false
    units: { min: 1, max: 12 }

  short:
    label: Short Firing
    description: >-
      Five Stages, no Charms, no overheating. A fixed shape for daily practice.
    seeded: false
    units: { fixed: 5 }
    disable:
      decks: [charms]
      counters: [calm]
    perUnit:
      - unit: 3
        skipPhases: [check]
        extra:
          - { do: resolveTarget, from: event }
          - { do: rollOn, table: setback }
      - unit: 5
        skipPhases: [check]
        extra:
          - { do: resolveTarget, from: event }
          - { do: rollOn, table: setback }
    notes:
      - Stages three and five always suffer a Setback.

  shared:
    label: Shared Kiln
    description: >-
      A pre-rolled Firing several people can attempt from the same seed.
    seeded: true
    units: { roll: d6+4 }

  pairs:
    label: Pairs
    description: Two potters, alternating who throws.
    seeded: false
    players:
      min: 2
      max: 3
      rotate: clockwise
      roles:
        - { id: thrower, label: Thrower, description: Makes every decision this Stage., acts: true }
        - { id: watcher, label: Watcher, description: Handles the rolls and holds the Charms. }

defaultMode: standard

hierarchy:
  - Charm
  - Overheat
  - Setback
  - Constraint
  - General rules

fixtures:
  - name: A quiet check leaves the board untouched
    mode: standard
    events:
      - { t: RunStarted, mode: standard }
      - { t: UnitEntered }
      - { t: SubjectDeclared, subjectType: Bowl }
      - { t: UnitFinalized }
      - { t: UnitEntered }
      # The Kiln Check phase closing is what advances the calm streak.
      - { t: PhaseCompleted, phase: check }
    expect:
      - { path: counters.calm, equals: 1 }
      - { path: subjects.length, equals: 2 }
      - { path: subjects.0.type, equals: Bowl }
      - { path: status, equals: active }

  # A play fixture: this one actually rolls the Kiln Check, rather than
  # hand-writing the OutcomeResolved it produces. A 30 falls in check-kind,
  # whose trigger rolls on Form -- so this is also the fixture that proves the
  # trigger still fires, not only that the state it would leave behind looks
  # right.
  - name: A 30 on the Kiln Check dictates the Form
    mode: standard
    play:
      - { enter: 1 }
      - { step: enter }
      - { declare: Bowl }
      - { step: work }
      - { finalize: {} }
      - { enter: 2 }
      - { step: enter }
      - { step: check, answers: { d100: 30, d6: 4 } }
    expect:
      - { path: outcomes.length, equals: 2 }
      - { path: outcomes.1.entryId, equals: form-cup }
      - { requests: answered }

input.command: cat packs/sketches/run-of-show.yaml

result.output:
# Run of Show: rehearsing a talk, a set, a show, one segment at a time.
#
# A Show is a series of Segments. Each Segment names its Bit, says how long
# it gets, and runs against that clock; a card drawn from a deck says what
# the room does to you while you run it. A Segment that runs its clock over
# owes the next one a cut. The main way to play is with someone else on the
# clock and the cards, the performers on a roster, and each Segment awarded
# to whoever landed it; alone, it is a rehearsal.
#
# Written to show a timer whose length the player chooses, an overrun that
# reaches forward into the next unit, a keyed table drawn by card rank, and
# a moderated mode as the default.

$schema: ../../packages/rules-schema/schema/pack-1.schema.json
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../packages/rules-schema/schema/pack-1.schema.json

schemaVersion: 1
id: com.scrthq.runlog.run-of-show
version: "0.1.0"
title: Run of Show
author: Runlog
description: >-
  Rehearse a show segment by segment. Each one gets the time you give it,
  a card says what the room throws at you, and running over owes the next
  segment a cut. Someone runs the clock; the performers are the roster.

category: practice
tags: [rehearsal, public speaking, comedy, stagecraft]

requires:
  - { id: material, label: "Something to rehearse: a talk, a set, a show", kind: other }
  - { id: cards, label: "A deck of playing cards, or one card drawn any way you like", kind: supplies, note: "Only the rank matters." }
  - { id: room, label: A room you can be loud in, kind: space, optional: true }

license:
  id: MIT
  redistributable: true
  holder: Runlog

capabilities:
  - deferredTriggers
  - counters
  - timers
  - journal
  - keyedResolution
  - moderated
  - clockRules

vocabulary:
  run: { one: Show, many: Shows }
  unit: { one: Segment, many: Segments }
  subject: { one: Bit, many: Bits }
  finalize: Next

unit:
  createsSubject: true
  min: 1
  max: 12

counters:
  segments:
    label: Segments run
    initial: 0
    incrementOn:
      - { on: unitFinalized }
  overruns:
    label: Overruns
    initial: 0
    incrementOn:
      - { on: outcomeResolved, table: overrun, cause: any }
    triggers:
      - when: { gte: 3 }
        oncePerRun: true
        label: Three overruns
        do:
          - { do: note, text: "Three Segments over. Cut a whole Segment from the Show before the next run, and say which.", persistent: true }

tables:
  heckler:
    resolution: keyed
    title: The Heckler
    description: >-
      Draw a card when the Segment opens. Its rank is what the room does to
      you while you run. A Segment landed on time is worth one; one landed
      through a heckle is worth two.
    entries:
      - { id: hk-a, key: a, text: "A quiet room. Land it on time.", points: 1 }
      - { id: hk-2, key: "2", text: "A quiet room. Land it on time.", points: 1 }
      - { id: hk-3, key: "3", text: "A quiet room. Land it on time.", points: 1 }
      - { id: hk-4, key: "4", text: "A quiet room. Land it on time.", points: 1 }
      - { id: hk-5, key: "5", text: "A quiet room. Land it on time.", points: 1 }
      - { id: hk-6, key: "6", text: "A quiet room. Land it on time.", points: 1 }
      - { id: hk-7, key: "7", text: "A question from the back, halfway through. Answer it in one breath and get back on.", points: 2 }
      - { id: hk-8, key: "8", text: "A question from the back, and it is a good one. Answer it properly, and still land on time.", points: 2 }
      - { id: hk-9, key: "9", text: "The projector dies. Whatever was on the screen, you are now describing.", points: 2 }
      - { id: hk-10, key: "10", text: "The projector dies and the lights go with it. Finish from memory.", points: 2 }
      - { id: hk-j, key: j, text: "You lose your place. Skip a beat forward and do not go back for it.", points: 2 }
      - { id: hk-q, key: q, text: "You lose your place, badly. Say so to the room, find it, and carry on.", points: 2 }
      - { id: hk-k, key: k, text: "The room is yours. Nothing goes wrong; make the most of it.", points: 1 }

  overrun:
    resolution: lookup
    title: Overrun
    description: Rolled when a Segment runs its clock over by a minute. What it costs the next one.
    roll: d6
    entries:
      - id: ov-cut
        range: [1, 4]
        text: "Cut two minutes from the next Segment. Decide what goes before it starts."
        triggers:
          - on: onEnterUnit
            label: Cut two minutes
            do:
              - { do: note, text: "Cut two minutes from this Segment before the clock starts. Say what went." }
      - id: ov-lastline
        range: [5, 6]
        text: "The next Segment opens with its last line. Say the ending first, then get there."
        triggers:
          - on: onEnterUnit
            label: The last line first
            do:
              - { do: note, text: "Open this Segment with its last line, then get there." }

phases:
  - id: open
    label: Open the Segment
    steps:
      - kind: declareSubject
        label: What is this Segment? The bit, in a few words.

  - id: length
    label: The clock
    description: How long this Segment gets. The clock starts the moment you answer.
    steps:
      - kind: actions
        do:
          - { do: prompt, kind: chooseValue, label: "How long is this Segment, in minutes?", options: ["3", "5", "10"], into: length }
          - do: branch
            on: length
            cases:
              - in: [3]
                then:
                  - { do: startTimer, minutes: 3, label: "Segment" }
              - in: [5]
                then:
                  - { do: startTimer, minutes: 5, label: "Segment" }
              - in: [10]
                then:
                  - { do: startTimer, minutes: 10, label: "Segment" }

  - id: heckle
    label: The Heckler
    steps:
      - kind: rollTable
        table: heckler
        label: Draw a card for the Heckler

  - id: work
    label: Run it
    steps:
      - kind: manual
        label: Run the Segment against the clock.
        description: The app cannot hear the room. It only knows what the clock says and what you tell it.
        checklist:
          - text: The Heckler was handled without stopping.
            shows: { table: heckler, scope: unit }
          - The Segment ended when the clock did, or before.

  - id: close
    label: Next
    description: A Segment a minute over its clock rolls the Overrun, and the next Segment pays for it.
    steps:
      - kind: actions
        do:
          - do: when
            all:
              - { clockRanOver: Segment, is: { gte: 1 } }
            then:
              - { do: rollOn, table: overrun }
      - kind: finalizeUnit
        label: Next Segment
        confirm:
          - The time it actually took is written on the run sheet.

journal:
  enabled: true
  prompt: How did the Segment land, and where did the time go?
  required: false

endings:
  - id: curtain
    label: Curtain
    text: The Show ran. Add up the run sheet and write the total time at the top.
  - id: cutShort
    label: Cut short
    text: Stop here. Whatever did not get run is first tomorrow.

modes:
  rehearsalRoom:
    label: The rehearsal room
    description: >-
      Someone else runs the clock and draws the cards. The performers are the
      roster, and each Segment is awarded to whoever landed it.
    units: { min: 1, max: 12 }
    moderated:
      contestants: { min: 1, max: 6 }
      award: first
    notes:
      - The moderator starts the clock when the performer starts, not before.

  alone:
    label: Alone in the room
    description: A rehearsal by yourself. Draw your own cards and be honest about the clock.
    units: { min: 1, max: 12 }

defaultMode: rehearsalRoom

hierarchy:
  - Overrun
  - The Heckler
  - General rules

fixtures:
  # A Segment on time owes nothing: the clock ran three minutes at most, the
  # Overrun was never rolled, and the next Segment opens clean.
  - name: A Segment on time owes the next one nothing
    mode: alone
    play:
      - { enter: 1 }
      - { declare: Cold open }
      - { step: length, answers: { chooseValue: "3" } }
      - { step: heckle, answers: { chooseValue: "7" } }
      - { step: work }
      - { step: close#0 }
      - { finalize: {} }
      - { enter: 2 }
    expect:
      - { path: clocks.0.label, equals: Segment }
      - { path: clocks.0.seconds, equals: 180 }
      - { path: clocks.0.status, equals: done }
      - { path: outcomes.length, equals: 1 }
      - { path: outcomes.0.entryId, equals: hk-7 }
      - { path: obligations.length, equals: 0 }
      - { path: counters.segments, equals: 1 }
      - { requests: answered }

  # A Segment that ran over rolls the Overrun, and the Overrun owes the next
  # Segment a cut. A scripted play cannot let a clock run that long, so the
  # first Segment here is the log such a Segment leaves; the second is
  # played, and settling the debt on entering it leaves the note to cut.
  - name: An overrun owes a cut next Segment
    mode: alone
    events:
      - { t: RunStarted, mode: alone }
      - { t: UnitEntered }
      - { t: SubjectDeclared, subjectType: Cold open }

One stage of the per-unit flow.

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | Unique among phases. Referenced by counters and mode overrides. |
| `label` | `string` | yes | Name shown to the player. |

| `steps` | `object`[] | yes | Steps performed in order. |
| `skipWhen` | [Predicate](#predicate)[] | - | Reasons to skip this phase. Any one of them is enough: a list of two means skip if either applies. Omit it to always play the phase. |

## `pack.phases[].steps[] (kind: rollTable)`

Roll on a table as part of the flow.

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `rollTable` | yes | Roll on a table as part of the flow. |
| `table` | `string` | yes | Id of the table to roll on. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Prompt shown with the roll. |
| `into` | `string` | - | Name to bind the rolled total to. |
| `optional` | `boolean` | - | Let the player skip this roll rather than requiring it. Default: `false`. |
| `skipWhen` | [Predicate](#predicate)[] | - | Reasons to skip this step. Any one of them is enough. |

## `pack.phases[].steps[] (kind: declareSubject)`
## `pack.modes.*`

A set of deltas over the base ruleset. Keeping modes as deltas rather than separate rulesets is what stops them drifting apart as the pack evolves.

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | yes | Name shown when choosing how to play. |
| `description` | `string` | - | What is different about this mode. |
| `disable` | `object` | - | Parts of the base ruleset this mode leaves out. |
| `units` | `object` | - | How long a run in this mode is. Omit to let the player stop whenever. |
| `seeded` | `boolean` | - | Pre-roll the whole run from a seed, so several people can attempt the identical sequence and compare results. Default: `false`. |
| `players` | `object` | - | Multi-player configuration. Omit for solo play. |
| `perUnit` | `object`[] | - | Per-unit overrides, for modes with a fixed shape,'unit three always suffers a consequence', and the like. |
| `clock` | `object` | - | This mode's clock on every unit, instead of the pack's `unit.clock`. |
| `score` | `object` | - | This mode's own score, instead of the pack's `score`. |
| `moderated` | `object` | - | Moderated play: one person runs the game on the device, a roster of named contestants races every drawn result, and the moderator awards points. Results with `points` are the challenges; everything else lands on everyone. |
| `notes` | `string`[] | - | Reminders shown to the player in this mode. |

## `pack.modes.*.disable`

Parts of the base ruleset this mode leaves out.

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tables` | `string`[] | - | Tables not used in this mode. |
| `decks` | `string`[] | - | Decks not used in this mode. |
| `counters` | `string`[] | - | Counters not tracked in this mode. |
| `phases` | `string`[] | - | Phases skipped entirely in this mode. |
| `moves` | `string`[] | - | Moves not offered in this mode. For a move another part of the mode already does: a race awards a challenge to say somebody finished it, so the move that said the same thing is a second way to do one thing. |

## `pack.modes.*.units`

How long a run in this mode is. Omit to let the player stop whenever.

| Field | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fixed` | `integer` | - | Exact number of units. |
| `roll` | `string` | - | Roll to determine the number of units, e.g. d6+4. |
| `min` | `integer` | - | Fewest units allowed. |
| `max` | `integer` | - | Most units allowed. |

## `pack.modes.*.players`

Multi-player configuration. Omit for solo play.

content.text:
Explored the pack format (`packs/demo/pack.yaml`, the sketches, the schema reference, and the four lists a shipped pack has to be named in). This is **bounded** — one new file in `packs/sketches/` plus registration in `check:packs`, `test:packs`, `scripts/seed-listings.ts`. Short design in chat, no spec doc.

I read `packs/private/` only to know what to steer away from. Here's the flag list you asked for, first.

## Entries worth having that sit close to the private pack

None of these reuse its words, and none would trip `tests/license-boundary.test.ts`. What makes them worth your call is that each is a DJ-domain restatement of a constraint that already exists there — a reader who knows both could call it a port.

| # | Candidate entry | Why it's flagged |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Only use effects you've already used this set. | Direct twin of an existing entry, domain swapped |
| 2 | Only use an effect you haven't used yet this set. | Same, the inverse pair |
| 3 | Pick one effect now. It stays engaged the whole transition and you use no other. | Same shape, one step more specific |
| 4 | No effects and no filter. Faders and EQ only. | The "no effects" entry |
| 5 | High-pass the outgoing track at 1 kHz and never bring it back. | Named-frequency filter instruction |
| 6 | Repeat the previous round's mechanic. | Structural echo of an existing entry |
| 7 | Free round. Mix it however you like. | The no-op result every table of this kind has |
| 8 | After the blend lands, roll d6. On 5–6, pull it back and do the transition again. | Post-hoc punitive dice on a finished piece of work |
| 9 | From the moment you touch the crossfader, you have 90 seconds. | Timer-on-commit entry |
| 10 | Say the transition out loud before you start it, then do exactly that. | Commit-to-an-idea-first entry |
| 11 | Break one convention of the genre you're in. | Break-a-convention entry |
| 12 | Match the groove of a track you already played tonight. | Mirror-an-earlier-subject entry |
| 13 | Play a track from earlier tonight, edited or pitched enough to read as new. | Reuse-a-finished-subject entry |
| 14 | Play the next track at least 6% off its native tempo. | Timestretch entry; also the neighborhood of your own 20-BPM example |
| 15 | Beat-match by ear. Sync off, waveforms covered. | Closest to a "mute the grid" entry |

My read: 7, 9, 12, 14 are generic enough to be table-stakes for any DJ pack and I'd keep them. 1–3, 6, 8 are the ones where the resemblance is in the *mechanism*, not just the topic. Tell me which to cut and I'll drop them without replacement rather than reskin them.

## The pack, in short

**Shape.** `run: Set`, `unit: Round`, `subject:` none — `unit.createsSubject: false`, no declare phase, journal off. One phase (`call`) whose only step rolls the style table, then `close` with a bare `finalizeUnit`. Nothing else per round, because every extra step is a press.

**Press count.** Steady state with auto-roll on is realistically roll → carry on → finish. I'll run it in the app and, if it's three, try moving the roll onto an `onEnterUnit` trigger so Finish alone carries the round. I won't claim one press until I've watched it.

**Style lanes** — one table each, one mode each, modes disabling the phases they don't use:

- **First Sets** — beginner. EQ swaps, long blends, one instruction per round.
- **Club Standard** — the working vocabulary. Double drops, echo-outs, loop rolls, key moves.
- **Turntablism** — scratch and juggle. Crabs, flares, transformers, needle drops, tone play.
- **Open Format** — genre and era whiplash. BPM jumps, hard left turns.

Difficulty rides inside each table rather than getting its own lane, so a beginner and a turntablist both get a table written at their level instead of the same table with a dial on it.

**Title.** `Fader Work`, sitting next to `Ladder Work` in the sketches. Alternative: `Deck Orders`. MIT, author Runlog, `category: practice`, `tags: [dj, turntables, streaming, music]`.

**Fixtures.** Two: a round that rolls and finalizes clean, and one proving a mode's disabled phases stay disabled.

Does the lane split and the title work for you, and which of the fifteen do I cut?

I agree with the assessment and split, as well as which to cut. For the name, I think "DJ Werks" (intentional spelling) is better than Fader Work as it's not clear that it's for DJs unless you explore the pack. I think we should also add this to the landing page persona list.
Cutting 1, 2, 3, 6, 8. Title is `DJ Werks`. Let me find the persona list.

# Practice Room: deliberate practice for any skill.
#
# An instrument, a language, drawing, a sport, code katas: anything you get
# better at by doing drills on purpose. A Session is a series of Drills. You
# name the Exercise; the Focus table says what to attend to this time
# (tempo, accuracy, feel, the hard bar); a Curveball sometimes changes the
# terms halfway; a Check-in at the end of the Session says how it went.
# Focus is the resource, it runs down, and rest gives some back.
#
# Written to show timers as the spine of a pack, a required journal line,
# and a run-end bands roll that says how the session landed.

$schema: ../../packages/rules-schema/schema/pack-1.schema.json
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../packages/rules-schema/schema/pack-1.schema.json

schemaVersion: 1
id: com.scrthq.runlog.practice-room
version: "0.1.0"
title: Practice Room
author: Runlog
description: >-
  Deliberate practice for any skill. Name an exercise, roll what to focus on,
  drill it against the clock, and let a curveball change the terms. Works for
  an instrument, a language, a sketchbook, or a sport.

category: practice
tags: [music, language, drawing, sport, drills]

requires:
  - { id: thing, label: "The thing you practice: an instrument, a language, a sketchbook, a ball", kind: other }
  - { id: timer, label: A timer, kind: equipment, note: "The app has one." }
  - { id: record, label: A way to record yourself, kind: equipment, optional: true, note: "A phone will do." }

license:
  id: MIT
  redistributable: true
  holder: Runlog

capabilities:
  - deferredTriggers
  - seededRuns
  - counters
  - resources
  - backwardTargeting
  - timers
  - journal
  - bandsResolution

vocabulary:
  run: { one: Session, many: Sessions }
  unit: { one: Drill, many: Drills }
  subject: { one: Exercise, many: Exercises }
  finalize: Log

unit:
  createsSubject: true
  min: 1
  max: 8

states:
  nailed:
    label: Nailed
    short: OK
    scope: subject
    description: Clean at the target. Move on, or raise the bar next time.
  shaky:
    label: Shaky
    short: SH
    scope: subject
    description: Not there yet. It comes back in a later Drill of this Session.
  warm:
    label: Warmed up
    scope: run
    description: The first Drill is done. Curveballs may now land.

counters:
  drills:
    label: Drills done
    initial: 0
    incrementOn:
      - { on: unitFinalized }
  cleanRun:
    label: Clean streak
    initial: 0
    min: 0
    incrementOn:
      - { on: unitFinalized }
    resetOn:
      - { on: outcomeResolved, table: curveball, cause: any }
    triggers:
      - when: { gte: 3 }
        oncePerRun: true
        label: Raise the bar
        do:
          - { do: note, text: "Three clean Drills. The next Exercise must be one you cannot do yet.", persistent: true }

resources:
  focus:
    label: Focus
    initial: 6
    min: 0
    max: 6
    step: 1
    display: bar
    description: Each Drill spends one; a rest gives one back. At zero, log the Drill you are in and stop.

moves:
  rest:
    label: Rest
    description: Five minutes away from the instrument, the page, the field. Focus +1.
    when: betweenUnits
    do:
      - { do: startTimer, minutes: 5, label: "Rest" }
      - { do: modResource, resource: focus, by: 1 }
  revisit:
    label: Revisit a shaky one
    description: Pick an Exercise marked Shaky and make it this Drill's Exercise.
    when: betweenUnits
    available:
      - { unitIndex: { gte: 1 } }
    do:
      - { do: prompt, kind: chooseSubject, label: "Which shaky Exercise?", into: again }
      - { do: note, text: "Name it again as this Drill's Exercise. Same Focus rules apply." }

tables:
  focus:
    resolution: lookup
    title: Focus
    description: What to attend to in this Drill, and nothing else.
    roll: d10
    entries:
      - id: f-slow
        range: [1, 2]
        text: "Slow. Half speed or slower, every repetition perfect. Ten minutes."
        triggers:
          - on: onDeclareSubject
            do:
              - { do: startTimer, minutes: 10, label: "Drill" }
      - id: f-tempo
        range: [3, 3]
        text: "Tempo. Find the fastest speed that is still clean, then sit just under it. Ten minutes."
        triggers:
          - on: onDeclareSubject
            do:
              - { do: startTimer, minutes: 10, label: "Drill" }
      - id: f-loop
        range: [4, 5]
        text: "The hard bar. Isolate the two seconds that break, loop only that. Eight minutes."
        triggers:
          - on: onDeclareSubject
            do:
              - { do: startTimer, minutes: 8, label: "Drill" }
      - { id: f-eyes, range: [6, 6], text: "Eyes closed, or away from the page. Feel where it goes. Five minutes." }
      - { id: f-record, range: [7, 7], text: "Record one take, listen or look back, then one more take. Compare honestly.", needs: [record] }
      - { id: f-teach, range: [8, 8], text: "Explain it out loud as if to a beginner while you do it." }
      - id: f-perform
        range: [9, 9]
        text: "Performance. One take, start to finish, no stopping. Whatever happens, happens."
        triggers:
          - on: afterWork
            do:
              - { do: prompt, kind: confirm, label: "Was it clean start to finish?", into: clean }
      - { id: f-choice, range: [10, 10], text: "Your choice of focus. Say it before you start." }

  curveball:
    resolution: lookup
    title: Curveball
    description: Rolled after the first Drill, at the start of each Drill. Most of the time, nothing.
    roll: d10
    entries:
      - { id: cb-none, range: [1, 6], text: "Nothing. Carry on." }
      - id: cb-shaky
        range: [7, 8]
        text: "The last Exercise did not stick. Mark it Shaky; it comes back later this Session."
        triggers:
          - on: immediately
            do:
              - { do: resolveTarget, from: choice }
              - { do: applyState, state: shaky, to: targetSubject }
      - { id: cb-key, range: [9, 9], text: "Change the terms: a new key, a new language register, a new medium, a weaker hand. This Drill only." }
      - id: cb-tired
        range: [10, 10]
        text: "It catches up with you. Focus −1."
        triggers:
          - on: immediately
            do:
              - { do: modResource, resource: focus, by: -1 }

  checkIn:
    resolution: bands
    title: Check-in
    description: Rolled once, when the Session ends. How it landed, dice and all.
    roll: 2d6
    entries:
      - { id: ci-low, lte: 5, text: "Heavy. Write down the one Exercise to start with next time, and stop thinking about it." }
      - { id: ci-mid, gte: 6, lte: 8, text: "Steady. Progress you cannot hear yet. Log it and go." }
      - { id: ci-high, gte: 9, text: "Good. Something clicked. Write down exactly what, because you will forget." }

targeting:
  strategy: playerChoice

phases:
  - id: curve
    label: Curveball
    description: Skipped in the first Drill.
    skipWhen:
      - { unitIndex: { lte: 1 } }
    steps:
      - kind: rollTable
        table: curveball
        label: Roll the Curveball

  - id: name
    label: Name the Exercise
    steps:
      - kind: declareSubject
        label: What are you practicing in this Drill? Be specific enough to know when it is clean.

  - id: focus
    label: Focus
    steps:
      - kind: rollTable
        table: focus
        label: Roll the Focus
      - kind: actions
        do:
          - { do: modResource, resource: focus, by: -1 }

  - id: work
    label: Drill
    steps:
      - kind: manual
        label: Do the Drill, with the Focus, for the time.
        checklist:
          - text: The Focus was kept for the whole Drill.
            shows: { table: focus, scope: unit }
          - Nothing else was practised in the time.

  - id: log
    label: Log
    steps:
      - kind: finalizeUnit
        label: Log the Drill
        confirm:
          - Marked it Nailed or Shaky, honestly.

journal:
  enabled: true
  prompt: What was clean, and what broke?
  required: true

endings:
  - id: full
    label: Full session
    text: Six or more Drills. Roll the Check-in and put it away.
    requires:
      - { counter: drills, is: { gte: 6 } }
  - id: enough
    label: Enough for today
    text: Roll the Check-in and stop. Shaky ones come back next time.
  - id: spent
    label: Spent
    text: Focus is gone. Roll the Check-in and rest properly.

triggers:
  - on: onEnterUnit
    label: Warmed up
    when:
      - { unitIndex: { eq: 2 } }
    do:
      - { do: applyState, state: warm, to: run }
  - on: onRunEnd
    label: Check-in
    do:
      - { do: rollOn, table: checkIn }

modes:
  session:
    label: A session
    description: Drill until Focus runs out, up to eight.
    seeded: false
    units: { min: 1, max: 8 }

  fifteen:
    label: Fifteen minutes
    description: Two Drills, one Focus each, and out the door.
    seeded: false
    units: { fixed: 2 }
    disable:
      tables: [curveball]

  hour:
    label: The full hour
    description: Six Drills with rests between. The shape of a proper practice.
    seeded: false
    units: { fixed: 6 }
    notes:
      - Rest between every second Drill; the timer is part of the practice.

  showPrep:
    label: Show prep
    description: A pre-rolled Session for the week before a performance, exam or match. Same seed, same drills.
    seeded: true
    units: { roll: d4+3 }

defaultMode: session

hierarchy:
  - Curveball
  - Focus
  - General rules

fixtures:
  - name: Two drills, one clean streak, focus spent
    mode: session
    events:
      - { t: RunStarted, mode: session }
      - { t: UnitEntered }
      - { t: SubjectDeclared, subjectType: "C major scale, two octaves" }
      - { t: UnitFinalized }
      - { t: UnitEntered }
      - { t: SubjectDeclared, subjectType: "Bar 12, left hand" }
      - { t: UnitFinalized }
    expect:
      - { path: counters.drills, equals: 2 }
      - { path: counters.cleanRun, equals: 2 }
      - { path: subjects.length, equals: 2 }
      - { path: status, equals: active }

# Forfeits: a penalty wheel for any stream.
#
# It names no game, because it does not need to. A Session is a series of
# Rounds, a level, a boss, a dish, a piece, whatever the stream is doing.
# Each Round spins the stakes, what the round is worth, and then the player
# plays. Every death is a press of "I died"; the third one puts the wheel on
# the board, and spinning it lands a forfeit on the round: off-hand only,
# no sprinting, muted for two minutes, chat's call. The forfeit holds until
# the round is called, then lifts by itself. Rounds called with no forfeit
# on them run a streak; five in a row is a clean sheet.
#
# Written to show four things the format does without a game behind it:
#
#   * a counter with a threshold trigger that rolls a table and resets
#     itself, so the wheel is a rule and not a reminder
#   * a move from outside the flow, "I died", pressed whenever it happens
#   * states that lift when the unit is left, granted by the table's lines
#   * a moderated mode where the same wheel lands on a whole roster
#
# Two things to know about the wheel. It is offered, not forced: the third
# death puts a "Three deaths: spin" button on the board, and the spin is
# the press. And it is offered once per round: a sixth death in one round
# does not put it up a second time.

$schema: ../../packages/rules-schema/schema/pack-1.schema.json
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../packages/rules-schema/schema/pack-1.schema.json

schemaVersion: 1
id: com.scrthq.runlog.forfeits
version: "0.1.0"
title: Forfeits
author: Runlog
description: >-
  A penalty wheel for any stream. Every round spins what it is worth, every
  third death spins a forfeit that holds until the round is called, and a
  streak counts the rounds you got through clean.

category: games
tags: [stream, penalty wheel, forfeits, challenge, moderated]

requires:
  - { id: thing, label: Something to be bad at on camera, kind: other, note: "A game, a speedrun, a craft, a recipe. The wheel does not care." }
  - { id: chat, label: A chat that can answer, kind: other, optional: true, note: "Two forfeits hand a choice to chat. Without one, they never come up." }

license:
  id: MIT
  redistributable: true
  holder: Runlog

capabilities:
  - deferredTriggers
  - seededRuns
  - counters
  - timers
  - journal
  - moderated

vocabulary:
  run: { one: Session, many: Sessions }
  unit: { one: Round, many: Rounds }
  subject: { one: Round, many: Rounds }
  finalize: Call the round
  terms:
    roll: Spin

unit:
  createsSubject: true
  clock: { kind: stopwatch }
  min: 1
  max: 20

# One state per forfeit, all in one group, so a round carries at most one.
# Each lifts when the round is called. In Chat's forfeits the round is
# everyone's, so a forfeit on it is a forfeit on the whole roster.
states:
  noSprint:
    label: No sprinting
    short: WALK
    group: forfeit
    until: unitEnd
    description: No sprinting, no dashing, no running for it. Walk until the round is called.
  offhand:
    label: Off-hand only
    short: OFF
    group: forfeit
    until: unitEnd
    description: Whatever you do with your good hand, do with the other until the round is called.
  chatsCall:
    label: Chat's call
    short: CHAT
    group: forfeit
    until: unitEnd
    description: Chat picks the next thing you do. Ask, wait, obey, then carry on.
  muted:
